A/starfish.subject: starfish
readings: side view top-arm tip (12,0.5) - same x as center, straight up
front view apex depth (z=10,y=0.5) confirming shallow Z thickness ~8 units
A/starfish.notes: Starfish (pentaradial echinoderm) modeled as a central disc (root, 'center') with 5 ray/arm leaves - no head or tail leaf per protocol since it has neither. The mesh's flat plane lies in X-Y (visible as the classic star silhouette in the 'side (XY)' view); the front (ZY) and top (XZ) views show the body is relatively thin in Z (~8 units), so Z-components of arm directions were set to 0, treating the animal as planar (ignoring the slight sculpted curl/pose visible in the renders, per 'proportion not pose'). Raw tip-to-center distances measured 11-12.3 units across the 5 arms; since sea star rays are anatomically equal, all arms were equalized to a proportional total length of 12 units, split into two inferred segments (base/tip) at the midpoint (6+6) since starfish arms lack discrete anatomical joints - this segmentation is an inference to satisfy the multi-segment/named-joint structural requirement. Two bilateral-looking pairs (upper arms B/C, lower arms D/E) were joined as symmetric leaf pairs; the topmost (dorsal) arm A is unpaired due to the odd (5-fold) symmetry. Draft render confirmed correct match to mesh silhouette and proportions - resubmitted unchanged.

A/octopus.notes: Mantle (bulbous sac) treated as the single 'head' leaf per convention since octopus has no separate head/neck; root placed at the arm-crown/mouth center. All 8 arms are anatomically near-equal appendages, but this individual's render shows them at different curl/pose phases (per Protocol rule 3, pose ignored for proportion) - raw top-view tip coordinates were mildly asymmetric due to curling and were symmetrized about the z=12 midline to derive 4 true bilateral pairs (A=forward-short, B=lateral w/ minor curl, C=posterior straight, D=long looping, matching the visible spiral loops in the side view). Each arm was split into 3 inferred segments (proximal/medial/tip) at roughly 40/35/25% of total reach, since octopus arms taper continuously with no discrete joints - segment count chosen to satisfy the multi-segment limb requirement. Curled arms (B, D) had their straight-line tip-to-center distance increased by an estimated compensation factor (1.2x and 1.4x respectively) to approximate true uncurled arm length. Head segment length/direction derived from side-view mantle peak vs. crown attachment point. Verified against rendered draft (top/side/front/isometric): head lean, forward-short arm pair (A), and increasingly long/curled lateral-to-posterior pairs (B,C,D) all match the original mesh's proportions and radiating arm-crown topology, so tree resubmitted unchanged.

C/starfish.notes: CORRECTION from previous draft: the earlier submission used raw grid-image delta-y directly as the world y-direction, which inverted the vertical sense of every arm (since the grid's y-axis is measured top-down in the image while the world frame's +y is UP). This produced a vertically mirrored starfish (arm1 pointing down instead of up, arms 4/5 pointing up instead of down) as seen in the rendered draft. Fixed by negating the grid delta-y for every arm direction so that arm1 (tip nearest the top of the grid, y=0) now correctly points toward +y (up), and arms 4/5 (tips near the bottom of the grid, y=22-23) now correctly point toward -y (down), with arms 2/3 pointing sideways with a slight +y (upward) bias, matching their tip y-coordinates (11 and 9) being above the disc's y=12. Subject is a radially-symmetric 5-armed sea star (no head/tail leaves per convention, root "disc" is the central body hub with length 0/direction [0,0,0]). The side(XY) view shows the full star clearly (arm plane = XY), while front(ZY) and top(XZ) views are near edge-on, both showing the same thin Z-band (6-18) that represents body-wall thickness/disc bulge, not additional arm length, so z-components of all arm directions are kept at 0. Each arm is split into two inferred segments (base -> tip) to satisfy the multi-segment/joint convention; true starfish rays have no joints, so both segments of a given arm share the same direction (straight tapering ray). Per instruction 3 (proportion, not pose), all 5 arms are authored with equal total length (base 3 + tip 9 = 12 units), the average of the 5 measured tip-to-center radii (12, 12, 12.4, 13.6, 11.7), even though the rendered pose shows unequal arm extents from bending/foreshortening. The 5 rays have odd radial symmetry (no bilateral pairing), so no symmetric-pair entries apply.
